question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(5n-3)(5n+3)}{n(2-25{n}^{2})}=\frac{25{n}^{2}-9}{2n-25{n}^{3}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{25{n}^{2}-9}{2n-25{n}^{3}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-25{n}^{3},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{3}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{25{n}^{2}-9}{2n-25{n}^{3}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{25{n}^{2}}{{n}^{3}}-\frac{9}{{n}^{3}})}{(\frac{2n}{{n}^{3}}-\frac{25{n}^{3}}{{n}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{25}{n}-\frac{9}{{n}^{3}})}{(\frac{2}{{n}^{2}}-25)} \\  & =\frac{0-0}{0-25} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $0.$
